speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing fatigue, weight loss, and jaundice. To understand the severity and cause of these symptoms, have you noticed any changes in your urine color or stool consistency recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old male. The patient complains of persistent fatigue and reports poor sleep quality. He mentions adopting a vegetarian diet in recent months to improve his energy levels but hasn't noticed significant benefits. The patient reports losing weight without trying over the last month.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the information; your age and unintentional weight loss alongside jaundice are concerning. Since you mentioned a recent dietary change, are you experiencing any abdominal pain, itching, or changes in urine/stool color?

REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Panel (LFTs), Bilirubin, Albumin, INR
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver Function Tests: AST-Elevated, ALT-Elevated, ALP-Significantly elevated, Bilirubin-Elevated; CBC: WBC-Normal, Hemoglobin-Normal, Platelets-Normal

speaker: Doctor
text:
The elevated alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin combined with normal white blood cells suggest a cholestatic process rather than an infection or acute hepatitis. Given your age, weight loss, and dietary changes, have you noticed any new abdominal lumps, or is your stool appearing pale/clay-colored and urine very dark?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Enlarged, thin-walled gallbladder. No evident stones.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound reveals a distended, thin-walled gallbladder without stones, which strongly points towards obstruction of the common bile duct rather than primary gallbladder disease. Given your age, significant weight loss, and the cholestatic lab pattern, do you have a history of smoking or alcohol use, and do you feel a distinct lump in the upper right part of your abdomen?

REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen with Contrast
REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Abdomen

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Abdomen with Contrast: No evidence of common bile duct obstruction or gallstones. Liver parenchyma shows diffuse uptake consistent with infiltrative process. A hypodense mass identified in the pancreatic head region causing compression of the distal common bile duct, consistent with pancreatic malignancy. No distant metastases identified on this study.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma of the Head. The CT scan confirms a mass in the pancreatic head compressing the common bile duct, explaining your jaundice, cholestatic liver enzyme elevation, weight loss, and fatigue.
